record.paper_title: Whitehead's Asphericity Question and Its Relation to Other Open Problems
record.original_question: Is the knot-like case of the Whitehead Conjecture, namely the case equivalent to finitely presentable groups of weight 1 and deficiency 1 having rational cohomological dimension at most 2, equivalent to the finite Whitehead Conjecture that every subcomplex of a finite aspherical 2-complex is aspherical, or is the knot-like case strictly weaker?

evidence.quote: whether this knot-like case of the Whitehead Conjecture is equivalent to, or strictly weaker than, the finite case of the Whitehead Conjecture

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A connected 2-dimensional CW complex $K$ is called aspherical if its second homotopy group $\pi_2(K)$ vanishes (equivalently, its universal cover is contractible). The Whitehead Conjecture asserts that every connected subcomplex of an aspherical 2-complex is aspherical. The finite Whitehead Conjecture is the restriction of this assertion to finite 2-complexes: every subcomplex of a finite aspherical 2-complex is aspherical.

A finitely presentable group $G$ has weight 1 if it can be normally generated by a single element, and has deficiency 1 if it admits a finite presentation with one more generator than relator. The rational cohomological dimension $\mathrm{cd}_{\mathbb{Q}}(G)$ is the projective dimension of $\mathbb{Q}$ over the rational group ring $\mathbb{Q} G$. The "knot-like" case of the Whitehead Conjecture is known to be equivalent to the statement:
$$\text{Every finitely presentable group } G \text{ of weight } 1 \text{ and deficiency } 1 \text{ satisfies } \mathrm{cd}_{\mathbb{Q}}(G) \le 2.$$

Question: Is the knot-like case of the Whitehead Conjecture (as formulated above) equivalent to the finite Whitehead Conjecture, or is the knot-like case strictly weaker than the finite Whitehead Conjecture?
artifact.status_search_result: The Whitehead asphericity conjecture (1941) and its finite version remain open, and comparison of the knot-like case with the finite case is an active question with no known resolution.
